facts: Q3 2025 EBITDA was negative $28 million, including a $20 million noncash inventory impairment, compared to negative EBITDA of $21 million in Q2.

Lower pulp sales realizations negatively impacted EBITDA by approximately $15 million, with the inventory impairment split as approximately $15 million attributed to hardwood and the remainder to softwood.
U.S. dollar weakness increased operating costs by almost $11 million compared to Q2 2025.
The company expects to realize approximately $30 million in cost savings and reliability improvements by the end of 2025 through its One Goal One Hundred program.
Liquidity position at end of Q3 totaled $376 million, comprised of approximately $98 million of cash and $278 million of undrawn revolvers.
Q3 cash consumption was approximately $48 million compared to $35 million in Q2, driven primarily by lower EBITDA.
The company's mass timber backlog of projects sits at about $80 million, with potential sales volumes from project inquiries in the last two quarters totaling approximately $400 million.
Planned 2025 CapEx spend is about $100 million, with 2026 CapEx expected to start around $75 million as the company prioritizes liquidity.
Canadian lumber now faces total duty and tariff impact of approximately 50% on average following Section 232 review, compared to 10% for European lumber.
The NBSK net price in China was $690 per tonne in Q3, a decrease of $44 from Q2, while North American NBSK list price averaged $1,700 per tonne, down $120 from the prior quarter.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $6.8 million compared to $8.2 million in Q3 2024, with Core revenue of $6.4 million versus $8.1 million in the prior year quarter.
The company executed a 34% global workforce reduction, bringing total full-time employee headcount to 89 from 133 as of January 31, 2025.

The restructuring is expected to result in $17 million to $19 million of annualized savings, including $13.6 million from headcount reductions and $4 million to $5 million from non-headcount cost reductions.
The company ended Q3 2025 with $158 million in combined cash, equivalents and investments with no debt, and expects to end 2025 with $152 million to $155 million.
Management expects operating cash burn of roughly $10 million to $15 million in 2026 following the cost reductions.
Five of 18 current clinical SPL programs are anticipated to enter pivotal studies in the next 6 to 18 months, with potential commercial launches in 2027 and 2028.
The company signed 4 new SPLs in 2025, bringing total signed SPLs to 32, and management expects to sign 3 to 5 SPLs annually for the foreseeable future.
CASGEVY delivered approximately $17 million in revenue for Vertex in Q3, with 165 people globally completing cell collection and patient cell collections per day doubling in 2025 compared to 2024.
CFO Douglas Swirsky will transition from his role in the first half of 2026, and the company has initiated a search for a successor.
The company reiterated 2025 guidance for Core revenue of flat to a 10% decline compared to 2024 and SPL program-related revenue of approximately $5 million.
Q3 2025 revenue was $4.6 billion, down 3.7% year-over-year, with unit volume declining 6%.
Q3 segment operating income was $287 million, reflecting a sequential increase of $128 million compared to Q2.
Goodyear reported a net loss of $2.2 billion driven by noncash items including a deferred tax valuation allowance and goodwill impairment in the Americas.
Goodyear Forward initiatives contributed $185 million of benefit during Q3 and are expected to deliver approximately $180 million in Q4.
Pro forma for the chemicals transaction, Q3 debt declined approximately $1.5 billion, reflecting asset sale proceeds net of fees.
Americas consumer OE volume grew 4%, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of OE share gains in that region.
EMEA consumer OE volumes grew 20%, representing more than 3 points of market share gain.
Americas commercial OE volume declined 33% as OEMs decreased production amid weakness in freight market conditions and EPA mandate uncertainties.
Annualized tariff costs are expected to be approximately $300 million, which is $50 million lower than previously cited after Canada eliminated tariffs on U.S. imports effective September 1.

For 2026, management expects Goodyear Forward carryover cost benefits of at least $250 million, raw materials benefit of $200 million at current spot rates, and tariff carryover headwind of $150 million to $160 million.
Net new home orders of 898 in Q3 2025 represented a 2.4% year-over-year increase and a record for any third quarter in company history.
Net income attributable to Green Brick decreased 13% year-over-year to $78 million, with diluted EPS declining 11% to $1.77 per share.
Homebuilding gross margins of 31.1% declined 160 basis points year-over-year and 70 basis points sequentially, marking the tenth consecutive quarter above 30%.
Discounts and incentives as a percentage of residential unit revenue increased to 8.1% from 5% in the prior year period.
Green Brick Mortgage closed and funded over 350 loans in Q3 compared to 140 loans in Q2, with an average FICO score of 740.
The cancellation rate improved to 6.7% in Q3 from 9.9% in Q2 and 8.5% in Q3 2024.
Total lots owned and controlled increased 11% year-over-year to approximately 41,200 lots, with Trophy comprising approximately 70% of this total.
Direct construction costs for labor and materials declined approximately $2,250 per home compared to the same period last year.
Construction cycle times decreased by 9 days year-over-year, with Trophy's average cycle time in DFW falling below 100 days for the first time in company history.
Total liquidity stood at $457 million at quarter end, with a net debt to total capital ratio of 9.8%.
Q3 2025 net product revenue was $150.5 million, up 31% year-over-year and 49% sequentially, exceeding the company's guidance range of $130 million to $145 million.
Advanced Wound Care net product revenue for Q3 was $141.5 million, up 31% year-over-year.
Surgical & Sports Medicine net product revenue for Q3 was $9 million, up 25% year-over-year.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $30.1 million compared to $13.4 million in the prior year period.
As of September 30, 2025, the company had $64.4 million in cash with no outstanding debt, down from $136.2 million at December 31, 2024.
The company amended its credit agreement on October 31, 2025, providing access to up to $75 million of future borrowings.
Full-year 2025 net revenue guidance was raised to $500 million to $525 million, representing 4% to 9% year-over-year growth.

The second Phase III trial of ReNu did not achieve statistical significance for its primary endpoint, though baseline pain reduction at 6 months was negative 6.9 compared to negative 6.0 in the first Phase III study.
The company has a meeting scheduled for December 12 with the FDA to discuss the ReNu BLA submission using combined efficacy analysis from both Phase III studies.

Management stated that over 200 skin substitute products will no longer be covered for DFUs and VLUs under the LCD scheduled to take effect January 1, 2026, while Organogenesis has 3 commercialized products on the covered list.
Q1 FY27 comparable sales grew 2%, beating guidance of ~1%, with revenue of $8.9 billion, an adjusted operating income rate of 4.1% (up 30 bps YoY), and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.28, up 11% YoY.

Domestic marketplace GMV reached approximately $250 million in Q1, and including marketplace GMV, domestic sales growth was more than 4%; full-year marketplace GMV is expected to be at least $1.2 billion, with Best Buy Ads collections expected to grow 10% to nearly $1 billion.

Q2-to-date comparable sales are up high single digits through Memorial Day, but full Q2 comp guidance is just ~1% growth due to lapping last year's Switch 2 launch (~$200 million in Q2 sales) and tough Win 10/back-to-school computing compares later in the quarter.
Full-year FY27 guidance was maintained: revenue of $41.2B–$42.1B, comps of -1% to +1%, adjusted operating margin of 4.3%–4.4%, EPS of $6.30–$6.60, capex of ~$750M, and ~$300M in share repurchases.
CEO Corie Barry will step down on November 1, with Jason Bonfig (current Chief Customer Product and Fulfillment Officer, 27-year Best Buy veteran) assuming the CEO role.

Best Buy will be the only national retailer carrying new RGB TV technology for approximately one year starting mid-June, supported by a major marketing campaign, with management noting it as the first material new TV display technology since OLED in 2013 and 49M TVs sold in 2020 now hitting a 5-7 year upgrade cycle.

Inventory was up nearly 8% and accounts payable up nearly 10% YoY, reflecting a strategic pull-forward of computing inventory ahead of memory cost increases; management expects blended computing ASPs to rise in Q2 and beyond with only muted unit elasticity, and no material supply constraints for FY27.

Domestic gross profit rate rose 20 bps to 23.7%, driven by marketplace, Best Buy Ads, and improved services, partially offset by lower product margin rates; international gross margin fell 50 bps to 21.5%.

Newer/emerging categories (AI glasses, 3D printers, trading cards/collectibles, health rings, PC gaming handhelds) doubled YoY, while computing posted its 9th consecutive quarter of positive comps and mobile phones its 5th, with Best Buy Business growing 15%.

Appliances continued to decline in Q1 but turned to demand growth month-to-date in May following targeted investments in pricing, marketing, availability, and delivery speed; Best Buy is also adding small (12K-15K sq ft) and medium (20K-25K sq ft) format stores starting this summer and converting space in 50 large stores into branded 'Meta Labs at Best Buy.'
Q4 2025 revenue grew 11.5% year-over-year to $14.88 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.96 also above the high end of guidance.

Full year 2025 adjusted free cash flow was $1.10 billion compared to $443.3 million in the prior year, with Q4 adjusted free cash flow of $1.63 billion representing the highest quarterly result in more than a decade.

Q1 2026 guidance calls for net sales of $12.45 billion to $12.80 billion (approximately 2.8% year-over-year growth at midpoint) and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.67 to $0.75, with gross margins of roughly 6.87% at the midpoint representing a 38 basis point sequential improvement over Q4 2025.

AI-related GPU and infrastructure project sales alone drove a negative impact of more than 15 basis points on Q4 gross margins, though these deals are low cost to serve and very working capital efficient.

Net debt to adjusted EBITDA leverage ratio improved sequentially from 2.2x to 1.0x, with total term loan repayments reaching $1.89 billion since the beginning of 2022, including an additional $200 million repaid in February 2026.

The company's intelligent digital assistant IDA enabled over 500,000 proactive engagements in 2025, converting over 100,000 opportunities into orders at nearly 3x normal conversion ratios, with IDA revenue expected to grow from mid-single-digit to double-digit percentage of total revenue by end of 2026.
Full year 2025 operating expenses improved by 47 basis points as a percentage of net sales to 5.0%, reflecting cost reductions and Xvantage-driven operational efficiencies.

Q4 gross margin declined 51 basis points year-over-year to 6.50%, driven by heavy sales mix toward lower-margin client and endpoint solutions and higher growth from Asia Pacific, where gross margins average roughly 250 basis points below the company average.
Self-service orders on the Xvantage platform were up over 100% year-over-year, while average revenue per customer on Xvantage increased 14% sequentially from Q3 to Q4 and over 30% year-over-year.

Q1 2026 guidance assumes no notable GPU deals, flat to low single-digit growth in client and endpoint solutions, low to mid-single-digit growth in advanced solutions, and double-digit growth in cloud, with management noting ASP increases are beginning to appear in Q1.

Q1 2026 revenue was $636.5 million, down 2.3% year-over-year (3.2% constant currency decline offset by 0.9% currency benefit), with the decline driven primarily by lower pass-through costs and continued FSP headwinds.
Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $47 million, up significantly from $30.3 million in the prior year period, driven primarily by cost savings initiatives.
Book-to-bill was 1.15x for the quarter and 1.05x on a trailing 12-month basis, marking the third consecutive quarter of book-to-bill at or above 1.1x, with backlog at $7.8 billion.

Fortrea reiterated full year 2026 guidance of $2.55-$2.65 billion in revenue and $190-$220 million in adjusted EBITDA, with Q2 expected to show a modest sequential revenue increase and slight EBITDA step-up.
Q1 delivered nearly $16 million in gross and over $9 million in net cost savings, tracking toward full year targets of $70-$80 million gross and $40-$50 million net.

Backlog burn was 8.2% in Q1, lower sequentially, driven primarily by previously communicated pricing concessions on a large pharma FSP contract that took effect in Q1 as a go-forward rate card impact.

Q1 operating cash flow was negative $17 million and free cash flow was negative $25 million, dramatically improved from negative $124.2 million and negative $127.1 million respectively in Q1 2025, with full-year 2026 still targeted to be operating cash flow positive.
Top 10 customers represented 54.8% of Q1 revenue, with the largest customer accounting for 17.2%, while DSO increased from 16 to 20 days sequentially but was 31 days lower year-over-year.

Management is targeting mid-teens adjusted EBITDA margin over the next 3 to 5 years (approximately 700 bps of improvement), with an Investor Day planned for the second half of 2026 to detail the margin progression.

Q1 authorizations skewed toward biotech and FSO over FSP, with significant year-over-year improvement in biotech bookings, strong double-digit growth in the China pipeline, and the best Q1 ever for clinical pharmacology authorizations since founding.
Disney Solitaire is tracking at an annualized run rate above $200 million, scaling faster than any title in Playtika's 15-year history.
Direct-to-consumer revenue reached a record $209.3 million in Q3 2025, up 19% sequentially and 20% year-over-year.
Q3 2025 revenue was $674.6 million, down 3.1% sequentially but up 8.7% year-over-year.
Adjusted EBITDA was $217.5 million in Q3 2025, up 30.2% sequentially and 10.3% year-over-year.
D2C represented 31% of total revenue in Q3, with a target to achieve 40% on a run rate basis within the next 2 years.
Slotomania revenue declined significantly to $68.5 million, down 20.8% sequentially and 46.7% year-over-year due to deliberate game economy rebalancing.
Bingo Blitz delivered record quarterly revenue of $162.6 million, up 1.5% sequentially and 1.7% year-over-year.

SuperPlay is currently tracking towards the 60% year-over-year portfolio revenue growth threshold over a $342 million baseline, which would trigger a 2x earn-out multiple on incremental gross revenue.
The company had approximately $640.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of September 30, 2025.
Playtika announced an expanded collaboration with Disney and Pixel Games to develop a fourth title in the SuperPlay pipeline.
Q1 2026 total revenue increased 11.7% to $789 million, with comparable center revenue growing 8.6%, slightly above expectations.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 18.3% to $227 million and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 160 basis points to 28.7%, though management updated the midpoint of full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 28%.
Adjusted net income was $96 million, up 27.4% year-over-year, while GAAP net income rose 15.8% to $88 million.

Average monthly dues reached $230 (up ~10.5% YoY) and average revenue per center membership was $930 (up 10.2% YoY), with the company ending the quarter at nearly 838,000 center memberships (up 1.4%).
Qualified medical memberships declined ~15,000 (-14.9% YoY) and now represent only 3.4% of total dues revenue, expected to fall to ~3% by year-end, while all other memberships grew 3.7%.

Management guided full-year revenue growth of 10%-12% per quarter, with total membership growth of 0.5%-1% in Q2, 1%-1.5% in Q3, and 2%-3% in Q4, and ex-qualified-medical membership growth of 4%-5% in Q3 and Q4.
Capital expenditures totaled $260 million in Q1, up 82% YoY, split roughly half-and-half between 2026 club openings and clubs being built for 2027 and beyond.

The company closed $200 million in sale-leaseback transactions in April and raised its full-year sale-leaseback target to $400 million, supporting positive free cash flow in 2026 with a long-range plan projecting over $400 million in free cash flow by ~2030.

Life Time has opened 5 of 14 planned 2026 club openings, maintains leverage well below its 2x debt-to-EBITDA target, zero revolver balance, and several hundred million dollars of cash, with a $500 million buyback authorization in place.

Management stated new clubs are generating cash-on-cash returns north of 30% in aggregate, with current per-club memberships averaging ~4,400 (intentionally lower than legacy ~11,500) to drive higher revenue, margin, and experience quality.
Q3 2025 revenue increased 13% as reported and 12% organically, with EPS of $3.40 representing 15% growth on a comparable basis.
Full year 2025 revenue guidance was raised by $43 million at midpoint to a range of $4.270 billion to $4.300 billion, reflecting 9.6% to 10.3% reported growth.
Full year 2025 EPS guidance was increased to $12.81 to $13.01 per share, up $0.33 at midpoint, representing 12% to 14% comparable EPS growth.
CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue grew over 10% organically in Q3, with U.S. up 8% and international up 14% (including approximately 1% benefit from equivalent days).
Over 1,750 IDEXX inVue Dx analyzers were placed in Q3, and full-year placement guidance was raised to approximately 6,000 units with instrument revenues expected to exceed $65 million.
U.S. same-store clinical visits declined 1.2% in Q3, with wellness visits down 2.5% and non-wellness visits declining only 30 basis points year-over-year.
Total premium instrument placements reached 5,665 units in Q3, an increase of 37% year-over-year, supporting 10% growth in the premium instrument installed base.
Gross margins were 61.8% in Q3, up approximately 80 basis points on a comparable basis, with comparable operating margin gains of 120 basis points.
Free cash flow was $371 million in Q3 and $964 million on a trailing 12-month basis, with a net income to free cash flow conversion rate of 94%.

Cancer Dx reached nearly 5,000 customers through October with over 17% of customers being competitive account adoptions, and Catalyst Cortisol achieved over 25% adoption among North American Catalyst customers within 3 months of launch.
Q2 revenue of $1.83 billion grew 6.3% on a core basis, exceeding the high end of guidance by 80 basis points, with EPS of $1.49 (+14% YoY) beating the top end of guidance by $0.07.

Operating margin expanded 130 bps YoY to 26.4% (180 bps sequentially), driven by Ignite operating system efficiencies, ~200 bps of strategic pricing (tracking to exceed the 100 bps full-year goal), and favorable Americas mix.
Full-year FY26 guidance was raised: core growth to 4.5%-6% (+30 bps at midpoint), EPS to $6.00-$6.10 (+$0.08 at midpoint, 7-9% growth), and operating margin expansion to 85 bps at midpoint.

Instruments delivered high single-digit growth with low double-digit growth in both LC/LC-MS and GC, supported by a ninth consecutive quarter of book-to-bill above 1 and a 200-300 bps replacement cycle tailwind.

China declined 9% in the quarter (worse than expected due to Lunar New Year timing and tough pre-tariff stocking compare), though H1 was roughly flat and management maintained its flattish full-year guide; China stimulus revenue is now expected to begin in FY27.

Forensics grew >50% driven by the TSA airport security contract (Agilent recognized $5M of the previously called-out $9M win this quarter), with bulk alarm resolution technology being deployed at FIFA World Cup host cities.

Diagnostics & Clinical grew 11% (vs. mid- to high single-digit guide), led by Omnis family double-digit growth in both instruments and assays, with the segment guide raised to mid- to high single digits.
CAM grew 8% (vs. mid-single-digit guide), with semiconductor representing ~30% of advanced materials and driving low double-digit advanced materials growth; CAM ex-China grew low teens.

Specialty CDMO (rebranded Advanced Therapeutics) grew high single digits with FY26 mid-teens growth still expected; Train C reached mechanical completion and is on track for revenue generation in spring 2027.

Food guidance was lowered from roughly flat to a low single-digit decline (Q2 was -3%) due to government funding delays in China and India and Middle East-related inflationary headwinds; A&G remained weak at -5%.
LKQ completed the sale of its Self Service segment to Pacific Avenue Capital Partners for $410 million, with proceeds used to reduce debt.
The company achieved $35 million in cost savings in Q3, on track to meet its $75 million cost savings target for 2025.
Full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS guidance was narrowed to $3.00-$3.15, with the midpoint raised by $0.07 on a like-for-like basis after adjusting for the Self Service sale.
Free cash flow was $387 million in Q3, bringing year-to-date free cash flow to $573 million.
The Specialty segment delivered 9.4% organic revenue growth, marking the first positive organic growth in 14 quarters.
Wholesale North America revenue decreased by only 30 basis points per day, outperforming repairable claims decline of approximately 6% by nearly 600 basis points.
Europe segment EBITDA margin was 10.0%, representing a 60 basis point sequential improvement from Q2 despite a 4.7% organic revenue decline per day.
Wholesale North America segment EBITDA margin was 14.0%, a 180 basis point decrease versus the prior year due to tariff-related pricing pressures and unfavorable customer mix.
Total debt was $4.2 billion with a leverage ratio of 2.5x EBITDA as of September 30, with an additional $390 million repaid on October 1 from Self Service sale proceeds.
The company returned $118 million to shareholders in Q3, including $40 million to repurchase 1.2 million shares and $78 million for quarterly dividends.

Q1 2026 orders were $18.3 billion, up 71% year-over-year with a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 2, driving backlog to $163 billion and accelerating the $200 billion backlog target from 2028 to 2027.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 87% year-over-year to $896 million with margin expanding 390 basis points, and Q1 free cash flow reached $4.8 billion, exceeding full-year 2025 free cash flow of $3.7 billion.

Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $44.5–$45.5 billion (up $500M), adjusted EBITDA margin to 12–14% (up 1 point at both ends), and free cash flow to $6.5–$7.5 billion (up from $5.0–$5.5 billion).

Gas Power gigawatts under contract grew sequentially from 83 to 100 GW across ~90 customers in 24 countries, with backlog at 44 GW and slot reservation agreements rising to 56 GW; the company expects to book 10–15 GW in Q2 and end 2026 with at least 110 GW under contract.

First-half 2026 gas turbine orders are expected to be priced 10–20 points higher per kW than Q4 2025 orders, with April quarter-to-date power equipment orders already matching all of Q1 2026 in value.

Power segment EBITDA margin expanded 500 bps to 16.3% in Q1, with 25 gas turbines shipped (+32% YoY); full-year Power margin guidance was raised to 17–19% from 16–18%, and Q2 revenue growth is expected at 15–17%.
Electrification Q1 orders rose 86% to $7.1 billion (2.5x revenue), with data center orders of ~$2.4 billion exceeding all of full-year 2025, and segment EBITDA margin expanded 590 bps to 17.8%.

Electrification 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $14.0–$14.5 billion with margin lifted to 18–20%; Prolec contributed nearly $500 million of revenue at just over 20% EBITDA margin since the February close and is expected to deliver ~$3 billion of revenue in 2026.

Wind posted a $382 million EBITDA loss in Q1 on a 25% revenue decline, with full-year 2026 EBIT losses still expected around $400 million; only 30% of onshore turbine shipments occur in H1, and Q2 losses are guided to $200–$300 million.

The company deployed $5.3 billion to acquire the remaining 50% of Prolec, returned $1.4 billion to shareholders (including $1.3 billion in buybacks), generated ~$900 million pretax from dispositions, recognized $4.5 billion of M&A gains, and ended Q1 with ~$10.2 billion in cash while remaining below 1x gross leverage.
Q3 revenue grew 34% year-over-year to $909 million, while adjusted EBITDA increased 15% to $214 million, representing a 23% adjusted EBITDA margin.
U.S. revenue increased 63% year-over-year and comprised 81% of Q3 revenue, with rest of world markets contributing 19%.
The company raised its fiscal 2026 outlook to revenue of $3.425 billion to $3.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $810 million to $830 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.26 to $4.36.
The Board authorized a new share repurchase program of up to $500 million over 3 years, representing the company's first buyback program.
The company exited Q3 with $953 million of cash and cash equivalents and no debt, and achieved a formal investment-grade credit rating.
Tariff impact increased to $44 million in Q3 from $33 million in Q2 due to the full quarter effect of tariffs that became effective August 15.
The newly formed Nextpower Arabia joint venture with Abunayyan Holding will supply 2.25 gigawatts of tracking systems to one of the world's largest utility-scale solar projects.
Year-to-date operating cash flow was $391 million and adjusted free cash flow was $360 million, with Q3 generating $123 million and $119 million respectively.
Fiscal year-to-date revenue increased 32% year-over-year to $2.68 billion, with GAAP net income of $435 million and year-to-date adjusted EBITDA up 22% year-over-year.

The company booked a 552-megawatt bundled technology order incorporating NX Horizon Hail Pro tracker, U.S.-manufactured eBOS, NX Earth Truss foundation system, and TrueCapture control system on a single project.
Q3 fiscal 2026 net sales increased 17.1% year-over-year to $135.7 million, exceeding company expectations.
Adjusted EBITDA was $16.8 million, up nearly 21% year-over-year, while adjusted EPS was $0.08 compared with $0.03 in the prior year period.
Handgun unit shipments into the sporting goods channel were up 28% year-over-year, with ASPs up 5.2% to over $419, indicating significant market share growth.
The company implemented an approximately 3% across-the-board price increase effective January 1, with no pushback from distributors or consumers.
Cash generated from operations was $20.5 million in Q3 compared with cash used of $9.8 million in the prior year quarter, a year-over-year improvement of over $30 million.
Debt was reduced from $90 million at end of Q2 to $75 million at end of Q3, with an additional $20 million repaid subsequent to quarter-end, bringing outstanding borrowings to $55 million.
Gross margin of 26.2% was up 210 basis points year-over-year despite a 160 basis point negative impact from tariffs.
New products represented 44% of handgun shipments and 28% of long gun shipments during the quarter.
The company expects Q4 sales to be up 10% to 12% over Q4 2025, with gross margin increasing by several percentage points over Q3 and a point or two over last year's Q4.

Internal inventory of $175 million was down $23 million versus the prior year Q3, while distributor inventory weeks of supply remained steady at approximately 9 weeks, in line with the company's target.

Q1 2026 net income was $31.3 million, or $2.53 per share, negatively impacted by placing a 9-loan relationship totaling $177 million on nonaccrual status (with $2 million of C&I and the remainder commercial real estate).

The bank has reduced the troubled relationship by roughly 50%, selling one loan at par for $9.4 million and two additional loans at par for $48.5 million on April 1, with two more notes held-for-sale being actively marketed.

Net interest margin fell to 3.457% from 3.74% in the prior quarter due primarily to a ~$3.4 million nonrecurring interest reversal, with management guiding to roughly 3.70% in Q2 (with March NIM already at 3.71%) and some tailwind expected from recouped interest on the April note sale.
Loan growth was a moderate 1.1% sequentially and deposit growth was 1.2% sequentially, with management acknowledging slowdown in demand and competitors pricing fixed-rate loans below 6%.
The bank repurchased approximately 400,000 shares of common stock at roughly $90 per share during the quarter.
March overall deposit cost was 3.10%, with $1.35 billion in CDs maturing in Q2 at a 3.89% rate, likely rolling to similar or slightly lower rates as repricing benefits approach stagnation.
Noninterest expense was ~$23.5 million in Q1, including over $1 million of elevated payroll tax from bonus payouts and stock vesting; Q2 run rate is guided to high-$22 million to low-$23 million.

Management's prior internal guidance of high single-digit loan growth for the year is now uncertain due to geopolitical risks (Middle East war) and policy changes, though they still hope for a growth year.
The balance sheet remains approximately 75% variable / 25% fixed-rate on loans and is now near rate-neutral, with large corporate interest-bearing accounts increasingly tied to Fed funds.

Resolution of remaining nonperforming credits is targeted through Q2/Q3 primarily via note sales when pricing is acceptable, alongside ongoing foreclosure and bankruptcy proceedings, with outcomes varying by loan-to-value and court rulings.
Q1 2026 total revenue was approximately $11.5 billion, up 1% year-over-year, with the growth portfolio rising 9% to $6.2 billion and diluted non-GAAP EPS of $1.58.
Management stated the business is tracking toward the upper end of its established full-year 2026 revenue and EPS guidance ranges, which were reaffirmed.
Eliquis revenue grew 13% to approximately $4.1 billion, aided by a Q1 wholesaler inventory build following the U.S. price reduction, which is expected to reverse in Q2.

Opdivo revenue declined 8% to roughly $2.1 billion, driven mainly by a U.S. wholesaler inventory drawdown to the low end of the typical range and continued conversion to Qvantig, which generated $163 million.
Camzyos revenue nearly doubled to $314 million with approximately 25,000 U.S. patients prescribed, and roughly 90% of patients remain on the 5 mg starting dose despite new competition from Aficamten.
Breyanzi grew 53% and Reblozyl grew 15%, while Cobenfy contributed $56 million and Sotyktu grew 20% globally.
Qvantig has achieved over 10% conversion from IV Opdivo in the U.S. in just over a year, with management targeting 30%-40% conversion within the next two years.

Gross margin declined 280 bps to 70.3% due to product mix, operating expenses ex-IPR&D were $3.9 billion, the effective tax rate was 18.3%, and operating cash flow was approximately $1.1 billion (reflecting ~$1.2 billion lower collections from Eliquis price cuts).

Iberdomide's FDA filing for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma received Breakthrough Designation and priority review with a PDUFA date of August 17, and mezigdomide's SUCCESSOR-2 Phase III hit a positive interim PFS readout earlier than expected.

The Librexia AFib trial for milvexian enrolled 20,500 patients with a noninferiority margin versus apixaban of approximately 0.83-1.3 followed by superiority testing on bleeding, with Phase III readouts in AFib, SSP, Cobenfy ADEPT (Alzheimer's psychosis), admilparant in IPF, and iberdomide PFS all expected by year-end 2026.

Amazon reported Q3 2025 revenue of $180.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year excluding foreign exchange impact, with operating income of $17.4 billion that would have been $21.7 billion excluding $2.5 billion FTC settlement and $1.8 billion severance charges.
AWS revenue grew 20.2% year-over-year to a $132 billion annualized run rate, representing the largest growth rate in 11 quarters and an acceleration of 270 basis points from the prior quarter.
AWS backlog grew to $200 billion by Q3 quarter end, with October deal volume alone exceeding the total deal volume for all of Q3.

Trainium custom silicon is now a multibillion-dollar business that grew 150% quarter-over-quarter, with Project Rainier deploying nearly 500,000 Trainium2 chips expected to reach over 1 million by year-end.
